title: Prevent duplicate token accounting for multiplexed streams on fallback/model-switch
creator: Ayesha Khanna
description:
Summary:
When a client uses multiplexed streaming (multiple logical requests over a single physical connection) and the request is routed to a fallback model (or retried on reconnect), we have observed cases where the metering pipeline counts overlapping token ranges twice: once for the original stream segments and again for resumed segments after the fallback/merge. This manifests as doubled billed tokens for affected streamed responses and causes billing disputes and customer escalations.

Background & reproduction notes:
- Occurs in scenarios where a single logical session is split across two model endpoints due to smart routing (latency/cost fallback) or region failover.
- Client reconnects or the router merges KV prefixes from the original connection into a resumed session.
- Current metering tracks per-chunk token attribution derived from per-stream chunk_ids + sequence offsets, but chunk_id reuse or overlapping offsets between original and resumed paths lead to duplicate attribution.
- Repro steps attached: traffic replay for session-id S-93 with controlled fallback to model-variant v2q -> v2q-fast; observer dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/meters/stream-duplicates?sess=S-93

Scope & impact:
- Affects multiplexed streaming customers with non-trivial reconnect/fallback rates (~0.6% of streaming sessions in last 30d).
- Billing discrepancy delta ranges from 1.2x to 2.4x billed tokens per affected session depending on resume point.
- High-priority because it directly impacts customer trust and invoicing.

Proposed approach (phased):
1) Detection: add a deterministic dedupe key computed in the ingress router for every logical output span: <session_id>|<canonical-request-hash>|<start_token_offset>|<end_token_offset>|<model_variant_tag>. Propagate this dedupe key through the streaming pipeline alongside chunk metadata.
2) Ingest de-duplication: extend metering ingestion pipeline (kStream consumer) to retain a short sliding-window LRU of recent dedupe keys per account (TTL = 5 minutes) and drop duplicates before token tallying. Store emitted dedupe keys in the fast in-process cache (rocksdb or memcached) to avoid cross-service RPCs.
3) Attribution correctness: when a resumed stream reports overlapping offsets, prefer the earliest-seen dedupe key for final billing. Ensure audit traces store both occurrences for investigation (not for billing).
4) Edge-case: when model_variant changes and tokenization differs, fall back to conservative counting heuristics (credit lowest common tokenization) and flag for manual review.

Acceptance criteria:
- No sessions in synthetic repro traffic produce >1x duplicate token counts due to resumed/fallback behavior.
- Dashboard metric "stream_duplicate_rate" drops to <0.05% within two weeks of rollout for traffic matching previous repro cohort.
- Billing pipeline unit tests cover chunk-id reuse, overlapping offsets, and model-variant tokenization mismatch with >95% mutation coverage for dedupe logic.
- Audit logs have clear mapping from dedupe key -> first_seen_event_id and second_seen_event_id.

Rollout plan:
- Canary (runtime-1.25-canary) with 5% traffic, observation for 48h, validate stream_duplicate_rate and CPU/memory overhead of in-process dedupe cache.
- Ramp to 50% after 72h if no regressions.
- Full rollout after 7 days with automated rollback on increased tail latency or CPU > +20%.

Telemetry & dashboards:
- New gauges: stream_dedupe_cache_hit_rate, stream_duplicate_rate, dedupe_cache_memory_bytes.
- Alert: stream_duplicate_rate > 0.2% for 30m -> page on-call.
- QA dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/meters/duplicates-qc?release=runtime-1.25

Migration & persistence notes:
- The dedupe key must be stable across a single session; ensure router canonicalization rules for request hashing are identical across regions.
- Backfill: retroactive correction impossible for historical invoices; include a customer credits playbook for affected accounts after validation.

Risks & tradeoffs:
- In-process dedupe cache increases memory usage on ingestion nodes; mitigation: LRU eviction and configurable TTL.
- False positives in dedupe when tokenization differs between variant models; mitigation: conservative heuristics and manual review flags.
- Latency overhead in metering path must remain <1ms p50; microbenchmark added.
